summary.text: In Japanese, 日 means “sun” and “day.” It is a whole-graph picture of the sun, not a compound of separate components.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts the sun. Early forms are described as rounded, with some squared because circles were difficult to carve; a central mark is said to distinguish 日 from 囗. The later Shuowen analysis divides it into 囗 and 一, but that segmentation is not established for earlier forms.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze examples attest 日 in early inscriptional traditions. The documented script traditions also include Chu manuscripts and seal script, but the evidence does not provide a detailed sequence of graphic changes.
The Han-era Shuowen account analyzes 日 as 从囗一, interpreting an outline and inner stroke. This is a later explanation of the graph, not proof that these were its original components.
Japanese standard references give 日 as the current form and identify no separate kyūjitai counterpart or 日-specific shinjitai change.

uncertainties.text: Shang-period inscriptions attest 日 for the sun, daylight, a five-day period, and a sacrificial name. They do not establish the order of these uses or all links among them.
The evidence does not date the rounded or squared forms or the central mark, or give a detailed sequence of their development.
Japanese historical examples do not establish a continuous semantic path from the early Chinese uses. The first use of 日 alone as an abbreviation for 日本 is also unresolved.

senses.text: Oracle-bone examples attest 日 for the sun. This is an attested use in the earliest documented corpus cited here, not proof of the graph's first-ever use.
Oracle-bone examples use 日 for daylight, including in contrast with evening. Whether this use developed from the sun sense is not established.
An oracle-bone example attests 日 in a five-day period. Its relation to the sun and daylight uses is not established.
The cited corpus includes 日 as a sacrificial name. Its relation, if any, to the sun, daylight, or day-unit uses is not established.

senses.period: Japanese word ひ; earliest cited example in 古事記 (712)
senses.text: A Japanese historical dictionary cites ひ（日） for the sun in 古事記 (712). This dates an attestation of the Japanese word, not the ancient Chinese graph.

senses.period: Japanese word ひ; earliest cited example in 万葉集 (late 8th century)
senses.text: A Japanese historical dictionary cites ひ（日） for sunlight in the late-eighth-century 万葉集.

senses.period: Japanese word ひ; cited example in 古事記 (712)
senses.text: A Japanese historical dictionary cites ひ（日） for daytime in 古事記 (712). This does not connect the Japanese use chronologically to Shang inscriptions.

senses.gloss: day as a unit of time
senses.period: Japanese word ひ; cited example in 三教指帰 (c. 797)
senses.text: A Japanese historical dictionary cites 一日 in 三教指帰 (c. 797) for a day as a time unit.

senses.period: Japanese word ひ; cited example in 竹取物語 (late 9th to early 10th century)
senses.text: A Japanese historical dictionary cites a specified-date use in 竹取物語, dated to the late ninth or early tenth century.
Japanese character-dictionary data lists Japan among the meanings associated with 日, but does not establish the history or first date of this single-character use.

senses.gloss: counter for calendar dates or elapsed days
senses.text: Japanese reference data records 日 as a counter for dates and elapsed days; it does not establish how this use developed from earlier senses.

limitations.text: Early inscriptions document several uses but do not establish their relative chronology or transitions. Shared early attestation does not show that one sense developed from another.
Dated Japanese examples attest Japanese words and uses but do not establish a continuous semantic path from the early Chinese graph.
The attested history of 日本 does not establish when 日 alone began to abbreviate it.

summary.text: 日 has the native kun reading ひ and the on-readings ニチ and ジツ. The official reading table also lists か. Readings such as きょう in 今日 belong to the whole word, not 日 in isolation.

readings.text: The kun reading ひ is used for the sun; 日 is also read ひ on its own.
A common on-reading in compounds, as in 毎日.
Another on-reading, used in 平日.

items.period: Mid Western Zhou attribution for the underlying form; the selected file is a modern drawing.
items.tradition: Bronze inscription form; modern vector redraw.
items.caption: This bronze-script form of 日, attributed to the mid Western Zhou 師虎簋 (集成4316), shows a rounded enclosure around a central mark. The graph is interpreted as a depiction of the sun; this image is a modern redraw, not the vessel itself.
items.alt: A thick, rounded enclosure surrounds a small central oval mark.
items.selection_reason: The visible rounded outline and central mark make this attributed bronze-script form a useful example of the sun pictogram. Its shape does not establish when those graphic details arose.
